sections.h2: Brazil's ethanol share has ranged from 18% to 32%, and 32% is temporary

sections.means: Brazil has mandated ethanol in petrol since 1938, and the 2024 law let the regulator move the blend within 22-35%.
sections.todo: The E32 decision should wait for the E35 technical tests the post says are still pending.

sections.means: Ethanol attacks seals and elastomers more than metal, so dispensers need metrology and UL certification before a blend is safe to sell.
sections.todo: Publish the outlet-level list of ethanol-compatible seal retrofits, as the post proposes for India's oil marketing companies.

sections.h2: India's E20 is behind Brazil's 32%, but its standards already reach E30

chart.title: Brazil sells 32% today; India sells 20% and has standards up to 30%

sections.means: India's dispensers are at an earlier stage than Brazil's, which built its certification regime over five decades.
sections.todo: BIS and Legal Metrology should publish a materials test standard and a searchable meter-approval register, as the post proposes.
